complaint.name: Synthetic Customer 047
complaint.title: [DEMO C047] Gmail attachment sends fail before reaching Google
complaint.description: Attachment sends fail with validation errors because the client passes a signed download URL as the attachment argument, while plain-text sends work.

hypotheses.description: Most likely cause: observed Gmail attachment-send failures in cedar were rejected locally because the attachment argument was a signed URL string instead of the required uploaded file object, so requests failed before any Google/provider call.
assumptions: Conclusion is scoped to observed Gmail attachment-send failures, especially cedar, during the incident window.
The controlled sandbox comparison isolates attachment shape as the discriminating variable, but supplied production records do not include a same-tenant successful plain-text Gmail send control.
The empty tool-executor deployment query does not prove no upstream caller/config change occurred; it only weakens an executor-rollout explanation.

hypotheses.description: Alternative, low-confidence hypothesis: an unverified caller-side or configuration change introduced the bad attachment shape, even though supplied records do not show a contemporaneous tool-executor deployment.
assumptions: A caller/config/schema path outside deployment telemetry could have started emitting string_signed_url.
This explains how the bad shape may have been introduced, not the immediate failure mechanism itself.

hypotheses.description: Alternative, low-confidence hypothesis: a provider-side Gmail outage caused the failures.
assumptions: Provider API is part of the normal path only after local validation succeeds.

recommended_actions: Synthetic telemetry indicates the immediate remediation path is to use the supported uploaded file object for Gmail attachments rather than a signed download URL string, and validate the serialized attachment argument before send. This action has not been executed as part of this report.

Collect missing canonical production telemetry for a same-tenant successful plain-text Gmail send or correctly shaped attachment send in the incident window to tighten the control set. This has not been executed.
Trace the caller/config/schema path that produced string_signed_url so the origin of the bad argument shape can be identified. This has not been executed.
Do not prioritize provider outage as the leading explanation for the observed failed execution; monitor provider health separately if broader concern remains. This has not been executed.
limitations: Supplied canonical records do not show a same-tenant successful plain-text Gmail send in the incident window.
Supplied records do not identify the exact caller/config/version that constructed string_signed_url.
Empty reproduce/retry/deployment scoped queries cannot prove absence of related events or changes.

findings.statement: Canonical executor logs for cedar show a Gmail request failing with status 400, validation_error=attachment_object_required, attachment_argument_type=string_signed_url, expected_attachment_type=uploaded_file_object, and provider_called=false, directly matching local attachment-shape validation failure.
The observed failed execution was rejected before provider egress because provider_called=false on the failing request, so this execution did not reach Google/provider APIs.

In the controlled sandbox comparison, the original request using attachment_argument_type=string_signed_url failed with provider_called=false, while the corrected request using uploaded_file_object succeeded with provider_called=true; attachment shape is the discriminating variable.

Observed production impact is concentrated in cedar: 738 requests with 420 failures and 420 blocked operations, queue_depth 132, p95 latency 1760 ms, versus maple with 604 requests, 0 failures, queue_depth 0, and p95 latency 160 ms.

A comparison tenant had a successful 200 response with same_provider_available=true and unrelated_read_succeeds=true in the same window, which is counter-evidence to a broad provider outage, though it is not a plain-text send control.

The supplied records show only an unrelated support-dashboard deployment near the incident window; they do not provide positive evidence of a contemporaneous tool-executor rollout causing this failure.

Do the canonical records support a pre-provider validation failure mechanism specific to attachment argument shape—distinguishing it from Google/provider failure, credential/auth issues, permissions, payload limits, or an internal regression—by showing failing requests rejected before egress while a discriminating control (same tenant/tool with plain-text send) succeeds?

objections: The candidate marks ev_370b5ecdbb78 as contradicting evidence, but that query returned no records; an empty partial reproduce search is not counter-evidence and should not be used that way.

payload.question: Scope and coordinate the evidence-led incident investigation.

followups.question: What canonical executor/request records exist for the failed Gmail attachment send attempts during 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z–2026-11-12T10:15:00Z, and do they show pre-provider validation failure versus any outbound Google API attempt? Collect null-filtered logs first, then narrow by tenant/request once concrete identifiers are found.

Were there any configuration, schema, toolkit, or argument-shape changes affecting the Gmail send action or attachment parameter handling near the incident window, and is there a controlled comparison between failing attachment sends and successful plain-text sends using the same tenant/account/path?

Does the evidence support attachment_reference_shape as the immediate failure mechanism—specifically that the attachment argument was a signed download URL instead of a supported file object—and what counter-evidence exists for alternatives such as provider_failure, expired references, permissions/credentials issues, or an internal regression?

notes: Current incident description is a hypothesis, not evidence; no canonical records are supplied yet.
Scope the observed failure first: identify affected tenant(s), request IDs, counts, and whether plain-text sends succeeded in the same window.
Prioritize canonical executor validation/error records over derived connection or refresh views.
Look for a discriminating control: a failing attachment send and a successful plain-text send, ideally same tenant/account/workflow, differing only in attachment argument shape.

Check whether any failed requests reached provider egress. If no outbound Google request exists for the failed executions, that would support a pre_provider_failure-style finding rather than provider_failure.
If attachment payload is captured, verify exact argument path and serialized shape before concluding argument_path_mismatch or attachment_reference_shape.
Compare latency and backlog only if observed in records; avoid inferring platform saturation without queue/worker evidence.
If signed URLs are involved, keep temporary_file_reference_expired as an alternative only if records show expiry/access failure rather than local validation rejection.

Investigate credentials and permissions only if the failed execution progressed to auth or provider initiation steps; do not require provider-side traces if the request demonstrably never left the platform.

Useful next evidence targets: request/execution logs, validation error payloads, outbound HTTP attempt logs, tenant-level success/failure counts, and any nearby deploy/config change records for the Gmail send tool.

payload.question: Does the evidence support attachment_reference_shape as the immediate failure mechanism—specifically that the attachment argument was a signed download URL instead of a supported file object—and what counter-evidence exists for alternatives such as provider_failure, expired references, permissions/credentials issues, or an internal regression?

notes: Evidence supports attachment_reference_shape as the immediate failure mechanism for the observed failed execution req-47 and likely for a substantial portion of cedar impact, but production coverage is incomplete because only one canonical failed request record is provided.

Counter-evidence to permissions/credentials issues is indirect but meaningful: the failed request never initiated provider work, and the validation error is local and shape-specific rather than auth- or grant-related.

Counter-evidence to an internal regression is limited: no relevant tool-executor/Gmail deployment is observed in the supplied records, but absence of deployment telemetry is not proof that no config or schema change existed elsewhere.

hypothesis.description: The immediate observed failure mechanism is local executor validation rejecting a Gmail attachment argument shaped as a signed download URL string instead of the supported uploaded file object, so the failed send never reached Google.
assumptions: The cedar failure pattern represented by req-47 is representative of the observed blocked attachment-send failures in cedar, but canonical production logs supplied here include only one concrete failed request record.
The empty reproduce search for 'plain-text' does not contradict the shape mechanism; it only means no matching reproduction record was returned for that specific search.

findings.statement: Canonical executor logs for cedar request req-47 show status 400 with attachment_argument_type=string_signed_url, expected_attachment_type=uploaded_file_object, validation_error=attachment_object_required, and provider_called=false.
The observed failed send was rejected before provider egress; the same canonical request record explicitly shows provider_called=false.

In controlled sandbox reproduction, the original request using a signed-URL string fails with the same validation and no provider call, while the corrected request using an uploaded_file_object succeeds and does call the provider.

Observed impact is significant but tenant-scoped in supplied telemetry: cedar had 420 failures out of 738 requests, 420 blocked operations, queue depth 132, and p95 latency 1760 ms, while maple had 0 failures out of 604 requests and p95 latency 160 ms.

A same-time comparison tenant shows normal behavior: maple has a successful unrelated request and zero failures, which argues against a platform-wide or provider-wide outage as the primary mechanism for the observed cedar failure.

actions: Pass a supported uploaded file object to the Gmail send tool instead of a signed download URL string, and validate the serialized attachment argument before execution.
Collect additional canonical production request samples for cedar attachment sends in the incident window to confirm how broadly the same argument shape accounts for the 420 observed failures.
After correcting the argument shape, consider replaying only the blocked operations that failed with this local validation error.
missing_checks: Need more canonical production executor/request records tying the broader cedar failure count to the same attachment validation error, rather than relying on a single explicit request plus sandbox control.

Need a production-side successful cedar comparator for the same workflow without attachments or with a corrected file object if available; current plain-text success is stated in the complaint but not shown in canonical production records.

hypothesis.description: A Google/provider outage or Gmail API failure caused the attachment-send failures.
assumptions: Elevated cedar latency and backlog could coexist with local validation failures, but they do not establish provider-side failure.

findings.statement: The observed failed request never reached provider egress; provider_called=false on the canonical cedar failure record, so provider failure is not the immediate mechanism for that execution.
The controlled reproduction shows the same request proceeds to provider only after correcting the attachment shape, which discriminates local argument validation from provider-side failure.
Maple had zero failures and a successful same-time request, which is inconsistent with a broad provider outage affecting all tenants equally.

actions: Do not treat provider failure as the immediate cause for req-47; only continue provider monitoring as background context.
If concern remains about mixed causes, gather outbound egress telemetry for other failed cedar sends to determine whether any separate subset actually reached Google and failed there.
missing_checks: Need canonical records from additional failed cedar requests to rule out a mixed incident where some failures were local validation and others were provider-side.

hypothesis.description: The attachment reference may have been time-limited or stale, but the observed failure was caused earlier by passing an unsupported signed-URL string shape rather than by expiry/access checks on that reference.
assumptions: A signed URL could also expire later, but no observed record shows an expiry or access-denied check because validation failed before any such step.

findings.statement: The canonical failure record identifies the attachment as a string_signed_url when an uploaded_file_object was expected; the recorded validation error is shape-related, not expiry-related.
Because the request was rejected locally with provider_called=false, there is no observed attempt to dereference or send the signed URL to establish expiration as the immediate cause.

actions: Prioritize correcting the attachment shape first; only investigate signed-URL freshness if failures persist after using the supported file object.
If needed, capture attachment lifecycle telemetry showing creation time, expiry, and any dereference/access result for future incidents involving temporary references.
missing_checks: Need canonical telemetry from a request that passes shape validation and then fails while accessing a file reference before temporary reference expiry could become a competing immediate cause.

findings.statement: The strongest direct production evidence is a cedar Gmail executor record for req-47 showing local validation failure on attachment shape: signed URL string supplied, uploaded file object expected, status 400, provider_called=false.
A controlled sandbox comparison changes only the attachment representation and flips the outcome from local validation failure without provider call to success with provider call.
Observed production impact is substantial for cedar and absent for maple in the supplied telemetry, indicating tenant-scoped disruption rather than platform-wide failure.
